identity.title: A strong magnetic field in the jet base of a supermassive black hole

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the Atacama large mm/submm array (ALMA), we have detected a polarization signal (Faraday rotation) related to the strong magnetic field at the jet base of a distant AGN, PKS 1830$-$211.

evidence.quote: PKS 1830$-$211, a powerful gravitationally-lensed AGN located at a redshift of $z = 2.5$ (cite: lid99)
PKS 1830$-$211, a powerful gravitationally-lensed AGN located at a redshift of $z = 2.5$ (cite: lid99)

question.value: Can Faraday rotation be detected at the jet base of PKS 1830-211 with ALMA, and what does the rotation measure imply for the magnetic field strength?

evidence.quote: Studying the polarization of this non-thermal emission from AGN is a direct way to probe the structure and strength of magnetic fields in the vicinity of a black hole.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00405.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00056.S, and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00020.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Sky frequencies around 100, 250 and 300 GHz; four spectral windows per epoch

evidence.quote: Our results are based on ALMA observations at sky frequencies around 100, 250, and 300 GHz.
The bandwidth in each frequency window is $\sim2$ GHz.
This detection has been possible thanks to the high resolution (sub-arcsecond) of our observations with ALMA

observing_dates.value: 6 epochs in 2012 (9 April to 16 June) and 9 epochs in 2014 (3 May to 27 August)

evidence.quote: one consisting of 6 epochs in 2012 (9 April to 16 June) and another of 9 epochs in 2014 (3 May to 27 August)
a powerful gravitationally-lensed AGN located at a redshift of $z = 2.5$ (cite: lid99)

what.value: Parsec-scale AGN core magnetic fields of ~0.05-0.10 G used for comparison

evidence.quote: where the derived magnetic fields have been independently measured to be $\simeq 0.05-0.10$ Gauss (cite: Gabuzda4; Gabuzda5)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Differential polarimetry on XX and YY flux ratios between lensed images, insensitive to X-Y gain/bandpass differences; no polarization calibration

evidence.quote: The estimate of $R_{pol}$ is, by construction, insensitive to bandpass and/or gain differences among the X and Y signals.
a new differential polarimetry technique, which we present in (cite: SupportA)

what.value: Observation details and ALMA project goals

evidence.quote: More details on these observations, and a summary of the main goals of this ALMA project, can be found elsewhere (cite: mul14).
fitted with the visibility-modelling software presented in (cite: UVMULTIFIT)

analysis_steps.goal: Measure flux-density ratios of lensed images

method.value: Fit XX and YY visibilities separately with a two-component model, bypassing imaging

evidence.quote: by fitting the models directly to the interferometric observables (i.e., the visibilities), hence bypassing the image deconvolution process.

method.value: Rpol = 1/2 (R_XX/R_YY - 1) with errors by standard propagation from fit covariance matrix

evidence.quote: The uncertainties have been obtained with the standard error propagation approach, using the uncertainties in $R_{XX}$ and $R_{YY}$

validation.value: Simulations with 1% antenna leakage give Rpol errors below 5e-4

evidence.quote: All errors are below 5$\times$10$^{-4}$.

method.value: Least-squares fit of Rpol vs lambda^2 and parallactic angle with a cosine model, for three epochs with quasi-simultaneous 250 and 300 GHz data; 100 GHz data excluded

evidence.quote: The parameter estimates in these three datasets have been performed by least-squares minimization, comparing the measured $R_{pol}$ to the model predictions.

assumptions.value: RMs and fractional polarization wavelength dependence similar for both lensed images, so p_dif and alpha are constant

evidence.quote: their rotation measures should be similar, as well as the wavelength dependence of their fractional polarizations.

fitting.value: Least squares; free parameters RM, p_dif and phase offset

evidence.quote: The parameter estimates in these three datasets have been performed by least-squares minimization, comparing the measured $R_{pol}$ to the model predictions.

validation.value: Monte Carlo with 10^4 random datasets; chance probability of equally good fit below 1e-10

evidence.quote: the probability that a random dataset allows us, just by pure chance, to get a fit as good as that from our observations is lower than $10^{-10}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Convert to rest frame and infer magnetic field

method.value: RM_true = (1+z)^2 RM_obs; compare with RM integral n B dl and parsec-scale AGN core RMs to bound B

evidence.quote: $RM_{true}$ is $(1+z)^2$ times larger than $RM_{obs}$.
$z$ is the redshift ($z = 2.5$)

used_for.value: Visibility fitting of flux ratios between lensed images

evidence.quote: fitted with the visibility-modelling software presented in (cite: UVMULTIFIT)
whereas between 0.8 and 1.6 mm$^2$ it is $70\times 10^{-3}$ mm$^{-2}$

findings_qualitative.value: RM increases at shorter wavelengths, so the Faraday screen lies close to the jet base and changes on sub-parsec scales

evidence.quote: The Faraday screen must thus be close to the jet base, and change substantially on sub-parsec scales (Fig. 4).

claims.hypothesis: Faraday rotation is detectable at submm wavelengths in the AGN jet base
claims.experiment: Differential polarimetry of the lensed images of PKS 1830-211 across 100, 250 and 300 GHz in 15 epochs
claims.result: Rest-frame RM ~1e8 rad/m^2 at 250-300 GHz, higher in 2014
claims.finding: Detected Faraday rotation, two orders of magnitude above previous AGN values

evidence.quote: Our estimated source-rest-frame $RM$s are about two orders of magnitude higher than the highest values reported previously for other AGN

claims.hypothesis: The Faraday screen is a distant external screen
claims.experiment: Compare Rpol derivatives vs lambda^2 across bands
claims.result: Derivative at short wavelengths much larger than at long wavelengths
claims.finding: RM varies with wavelength so the screen is near the jet base

evidence.quote: the different derivatives of $R_{pol}$ vs. $\lambda^2$ must be due to larger $RM$ at shorter wavelengths

claims.hypothesis: Magnetic field strength at the sub-parsec jet base
claims.result: RM ~1e5 times larger than parsec-scale cores
claims.finding: Fields of at least a few tens of Gauss

evidence.quote: this suggests that the magnetic fields in the sub-parsec regions we are probing are at least a few tens of Gauss, and possibly much higher.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: External spherically symmetric accreting screen or external clouds rejected as the origin of the RM

evidence.quote: Our finding cannot be explained easily if the $RM$ is only caused by an external (e.g. spherically symmetric) screen of material

limitations_admitted.value: B, electron density and path length cannot be disentangled from the RM

evidence.quote: it is impossible to unambiguously disentangle the contributions of the magnetic field, electron density and path length

referee_caveats_inferred: Only three epochs have quasi-simultaneous 250/300 GHz data for the fit; the RM-only fit has 3 free parameters
Interpretation depends on assumption that both lensed images share the same RM
Time delay between images and source variability may bias p_dif and phase
The B-field limit relies on scaling from parsec-scale cores
